title: The unit-normalized internal-Hom comparison for an isomorphic base change
statement: Let g:X→Y be a scheme isomorphism, O a commutative ring sheaf on Y_proet, and F,G O-module sheaves. Use the inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and internal Hom of [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. There are isomorphisms η(F,G):g⁻¹Hom_O(F,G)≅Hom_{g⁻¹O}(g⁻¹F,g⁻¹G). For arrows a:W→V, a Hom section φ over V and s∈F(W), η sends the unit section of φ to the transformation taking the unit section of s at g*W→g*V to the unit section of φ_a(s). These isomorphisms are natural contravariantly in F and covariantly in G: the square induced by every a:F'→F and b:G→G' commutes. The unit-section and mixed-universe conventions are those of [def-pur-inverse-image-tensor-hom-sections].

source.place: Tags 04IX, 04TT and 0GMX; inverse site equivalence, not the finite-presentation lemma 0GN2

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] to see that base change is an equivalence of sites and that the ring adjunction unit is invertible. On presheaf internal Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom], precomposition along the induced slice equivalence [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] is bijective: the inverse is the preimage under the fully faithful reindexing functor, and linearity descends by essential surjectivity. Restriction of scalars along the invertible ring unit likewise gives a bijection of linear natural transformations. Together these yield the pushforward Hom comparison. Use the canonical adjunction and its unit-section formula from [new-lem-weil-pbc-proetale-module-canonical-unit]; The arbitrary-adjunction comparison [new-lem-weil-pbc-proetale-module-inverse-image-unit-comparison] identifies the forgotten module unit with an invertible abelian unit followed by an invertible comparison; the faithful forgetful functor reflects its invertibility. The abelian site equivalence also makes module pushforward reflect isomorphisms. Conjugate Hom by the module units and take the adjunction mate to construct the inverse-image comparison. The unit identity proves it invertible after pushforward. Evaluation on a slice arrow gives the stated section formula, and unit naturality together with pre- and postcomposition gives two-variable naturality. The empty site and zero ring require no exception.
